## Fast-slow system {.center .r-stack}
  $$ 
  \begin{cases} 
    \dot X^\epsilon_t = f(X^\epsilon_t, Y^\epsilon_t)  \\  
    \epsilon \dot Y_t = g(X^\epsilon_t, Y^\epsilon_t) + \sqrt{\epsilon} \sigma(X^\epsilon_t, Y^\epsilon_t) \, dW_t 
  \end{cases}
  $$



## Can we approximate the system efficiently? {.center}


## Averaging Principle
<section>
  <div class="fragment">
  Under suitable conditions, $X^\epsilon_t$ is approximated by solution of
  $$
  \dot  X_t = F(  X_t )
  $$
  for an appropriate $F$ (some sort of averaging over $y$).
  </div>
</section>
